long_biography.plain_text:
Blum entered business through MicroBanks, a memory-module company begun with a loan from his adoptive father. He sold it while still in his early twenties, then co-founded Pinnacle Micro with his father before establishing Buy.com in 1997. His controlling stake and subsequent share sales gave him substantial capital for later ventures.

After returning to lead Buy.com, Blum also managed ThinkTank Holdings, an investment fund that backed technology ventures. His later work combines private investment with company creation. Through Dutch Design, an Amsterdam marine studio, he has applied that founder-led approach to a new design business while retaining active investment vehicles.

Public sources do not disclose the present value of each interest. Finance & Investments is selected because the SEC defines ThinkTank as his private-equity fund and current official filings establish continuing investment and family-office vehicles; the newer studio is retained in biography without allowing yacht-adjacent visibility to determine the wealth classification.

Blum personally founded and sold MicroBanks and later founded Buy.com, establishing built rather than inherited wealth. The Los Angeles Times also documents a $17,000 loan from his adoptive father for MicroBanks and father-son formation of Pinnacle Micro. That positive family-capital and collaboration evidence supports Self-made — advantaged start rather than independent start or a vague broad category.

The SEC documented ThinkTank's historic ownership, private-equity mandate and managing-partner role. Florida's register shows an active same-name entity with Scott Blum as manager and the same federal employer-identification number reported for the current registration, but it does not disclose assets or portfolio composition. The dossier therefore classifies the current sector without inventing fund size, returns or holdings.

E-commerce directly captures the platform that created Blum's principal documented wealth. Private equity captures his separately evidenced long-term ThinkTank mandate and current vehicle continuity.
